official.deadline_note: Stage 1 concept notes are due 23:59 GMT on Friday 30 October 2026; late, incomplete or ineligible submissions will not be considered. Only the highest-scoring concept notes per region are shortlisted and notified (by end of December 2026) and are then invited to submit a full application through the CLP online application portal; no Stage 2 deadline date and no separate institutional deadline are published.
official.status_note: The call for applications to the CLP Future Conservationist Awards 2027 is open; concept notes must be submitted by Friday, October 30, 2026 (23:59 GMT).
official.tuition_coverage_note: CLP funding cannot be used to cover costs relating to tuition fees, conferences or scholarships (published in the CLP FAQs).
benefits: Project grant of up to US$15,000 for the proposed conservation project
Ongoing support through CLP's global Alumni Network, including funding, training and mentorship
Long-term backing and advisory support from CLP staff and partner organisations
One representative from each winning team invited to an international training event organised by CLP; CLP covers all reasonable costs of the training
Winning projects can become eligible for continued support through CLP's Continuation Awards and Alumni Network
eligibility: CLP Awards are for team-based conservation projects; each team must have at least three people

All team members must be nationals of the country where the project is taking place; in special cases one team member can be a non-national subject to clear justification of the expertise brought, and should be a national of an eligible country

All team members must be early-career conservationists with no more than five years of paid conservation experience (degree research, unpaid volunteering and internships do not count); applicants currently enrolled in a PhD programme are not eligible

No team member can be a part- or full-time paid employee or contractor with a CLP partner organisation (BirdLife International, Fauna & Flora, Wildlife Conservation Society); applicants can participate in only one CLP project at a time

Project duration must be at least six months and no more than one year, and the total funding request from CLP must not exceed US$15,000, with CLP funding covering at least 50% of the total project budget

The project must take place in one of the eligible low- and middle-income countries in Africa, Asia, the Pacific, Latin America and the Caribbean, Eastern and South-eastern Europe and the Middle East; some high-income Global-South countries are eligible and a full list of ineligible countries is published
requirements: Submit a concept note completed on the official downloadable CLP concept note template, in English, by email to clp.applications@birdlife.org
Follow the 2027 concept note guidelines, including the eligibility criteria and the list of ineligible countries
Demonstrate that the proposed project goes beyond academic research being carried out for any team member's degree
Explain how each team member will develop their capacity through the project
Provide an itemised budget; justification must be given for any individual item over US$1,000
Provide evidence of early-career status, for example a detailed employment history on the application form
documents: Stage 1: completed concept note on the official CLP concept note template (submitted by email)
Stage 2: full application via the CLP online application portal, for shortlisted applicants only, with detailed guidelines provided at that stage
Evidence of early-career status such as a detailed employment history
selection_criteria: Concept notes are assessed and scored by global experts on four main criteria: Feasibility, Technical Capacity to Deliver the Objectives, Conservation Impact, and Contribution to Diversity, Equity and Inclusion (DEI)
A focused, high-priority conservation project combining a balance of research and conservation action
Contribution to the long-term success of local conservation efforts and to the inclusion, capacity building and awareness of local stakeholders
Realistic, cost-effective objectives with SMART goals and appropriate methods, activities and budget

Work at priority conservation sites (e.g. Alliance for Zero Extinction sites, Important Bird and Biodiversity Areas, Key Biodiversity Areas, Ramsar sites, UNESCO World Heritage Sites, Marine Protected Areas) is looked on favourably
The proposal must be written by the applicants themselves; proposals with excessive AI-generated answers are unlikely to be funded
coverage: Project grant of up to US$15,000 towards the costs of the proposed conservation project
The budget must be itemised; any individual item over US$1,000 must be justified, and major budget sections must be broken down in detail

CLP does not fund: conference attendance, tuition fees for academic programs or scholarships, the cost of consultants, projects initiated by a CLP partner organisation, gene storage, invasive methods or captive breeding of animals
Per diems for team members can be covered but not consultants; laboratory analyses must be justified as critical and urgent for conservation
Grants are dispersed in two instalments, with 85% of the grant provided at the start and the remaining 15% once reporting requirements are met
application_method: Read the 2027 guidelines and check that your country is not on the published list of ineligible countries
Download and complete the official concept note template in English
Email the completed concept note to clp.applications@birdlife.org by 23:59 GMT on Friday 30 October 2026
Await notification; only the highest-scoring concept notes per region are contacted (by end of December 2026)
If shortlisted, submit the full application through the CLP online application portal following the Stage 2 guidelines
official.application_route: Email the completed English concept note template to clp.applications@birdlife.org by 23:59 GMT on 30 October 2026; shortlisted teams are then invited to submit a full application via the CLP online application portal.
official.citizenship_residency: All team members must be nationals of the country in which the project will take place; one team member can be a non-national if the expertise brought to the team is clearly justified, and should be a national of an eligible country.
official.international_eligibility: Open to teams in eligible low- and middle-income countries in Africa, Asia, the Pacific, Latin America and the Caribbean, Eastern and South-eastern Europe and the Middle East, plus some high-income Global-South countries; nationals of listed high-income countries and of countries under UN/EU/UK/USA sanctions regimes are not eligible.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Projects must address globally important, at-risk habitats and species through ecological research and conservation action within one of eight themes: a) climate impact and adaptation, b) biodiversity conservation, c) habitat restoration and/or management, d) social development and wellbeing, e) Indigenous community participation and/or community-led conservation, f) environmental policy, g) human-wildlife conflict, or h) environmental education and citizen science. 'At-risk' species are those categorised by the IUCN Red List as globally threatened (CR, EN, VU) or Data Deficient, or where information indicates the need for urgent local conservation action.
official.research_requirement: Proposed projects must go beyond academic research being carried out for any team member's degree; work done for an undergraduate or master's degree is eligible, but projects tied directly to a PhD or doctoral research are ineligible. Projects must combine a balance of research and conservation action.
official.duration: Project duration must be at least six months and no more than one year (6-12 months).
official.description: CLP offers Future Conservationist Awards of up to US$15,000 each to conduct scientific research, encourage and promote pro-conservation attitudes and deliver tangible results to better conserve and manage the natural world, developing the leadership capacity of early-career conservationists working in teams. As a partnership initiative between BirdLife International, Fauna & Flora and the Wildlife Conservation Society, CLP provides financial support, ongoing mentorship, knowledge exchange and networking opportunities.
official.region: Global (eligible low- and middle-income countries; Global South focus)
official.program_type: Team conservation project grant (Conservation Leadership Programme)
official.english_requirement: Concept notes and applications must be completed in English; there is no published test score requirement. CLP recommends having an advisor or English-speaking person review the concept note before submission.

applicant_utility.summary: Build a team of at least three nationals of your project country, each with no more than five years of paid conservation experience, and send the completed English concept note on CLP's official template to clp.applications@birdlife.org before 23:59 GMT on Friday 30 October 2026. Your request from CLP can be at most US$15,000 and must fund at least half of the total project budget, so line up co-funding or in-kind contributions before you build the budget. Only the highest-scoring concept notes per region advance to the Stage 2 full application, so the concept note has to stand on its own; you will hear whether you are shortlisted by the end of December 2026.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Early-career, in-country conservation teams in low- and middle-income countries who can deliver a 6-12 month applied project on a globally threatened species or habitat and already share half of the project cost from other sources.
application_readiness_checklist: Check your country against the published ineligible-countries list, and if your nationality is on the 'contact CLP first' list, email CLP before drafting anything

Confirm every team member's paid conservation experience totals five years or less, that nobody is enrolled in a PhD programme, and that nobody works or contracts for BirdLife International, Fauna & Flora or WCS
Verify the target species' current IUCN Red List status, or gather peer-reviewed evidence that urgent local conservation action is needed
Draft an itemised budget with every item over US$1,000 justified, keeping the CLP request at or under US$15,000 and at 50% or more of the total
Frame the work as new, applied conservation that clearly exceeds any degree-related research, and state how each member's skills will grow
Have a strong English speaker proofread the concept note, then send it early enough to confirm CLP received it before the GMT cutoff
common_rejection_risks: Concept note arrives late, incomplete or off-template - late, incomplete or ineligible submissions are not considered at all
The project reads as a continuation of an existing initiative, or is essentially PhD or thesis data collection without additional conservation action

A team member exceeds five years of paid conservation experience, is a national of the project's high-income country without justification, or is on the staff or contractor list of a CLP partner organisation
Target species is only Near Threatened or Least Concern with no evidence of urgent conservation need, or the budget leans on laboratory work that is never justified as critical
The CLP request exceeds US$15,000 or falls below 50% of the total budget, leaving the co-funding gap unexplained
The concept note appears AI-generated, or omits how each team member will build capacity
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: CLP funds at most US$15,000 and must cover at least half of the budget, so the team must raise or contribute the remainder from other donors. Conference attendance, tuition fees, scholarships, consultant fees, gene storage, invasive methods and captive breeding are never funded, and the final 15% of the grant is only released after reporting requirements are met. Winning teams send one representative to CLP's international training event, whose reasonable costs CLP covers separately from the project budget.
document_audit: Use the current official template (Concept Note Team Awards 2027) downloaded from the award page, not an older year's version
Incomplete concept notes are rejected outright, so answer every question on the template before submitting
Submission is by email only at Stage 1 - delivery failure is your risk, so keep the sent message and ask for acknowledgement if you have not heard back
Prepare a detailed employment history for each member, as early-career status must be evidenced on the application form
If shortlisted, the full application moves to the CLP online portal, so check that the mailbox you list is monitored and that a nominated lead can handle portal access
alerts: The Stage 1 cutoff is 23:59 GMT on Friday 30 October 2026 with no late or incomplete submissions accepted, and GMT is not local time for most applicants
Only the top-scoring concept notes per region advance, unsuccessful teams are not contacted individually unless they ask, and shortlisted teams hear by end of December 2026
Applicants can hold only one active CLP project at a time, and no more than three Future Conservationist projects in total with only one as team leader
Nationals of several listed countries (e.g. Afghanistan, DRC, Haiti, Mali, Myanmar, Venezuela, Zimbabwe) must contact CLP before applying because of sanctions and restricted-party regimes
A live applicant Q&A session is scheduled for 20 October 2026, and CLP staff support stops two weeks before the deadline
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Email the completed English concept note template to clp.applications@birdlife.org by 23:59 GMT on 30 October 2026; CLP scores concept notes, notifies shortlisted teams by end of December 2026, and those teams then submit the full application through the online portal.
